subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Acme Health

Hi Samir / Priya -

Thanks again for the call earlier - appreciate you walking through the inference workload and latency needs. Below is a short recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points / goals
- Current production latency spikes at peak traffic (p95 ~450ms) and intermittent queueing during morning batch windows.
- Data isolation requirement: PHI/PII must remain in a customer VPC and logs retained per Acme policy.
- Peak throughput target: ~600 tokens/sec sustained, with bursts to 2.5k tokens/sec for short periods.
- Primary objective: predictable per-token cost while meeting p99 latency SLA and 99.95% uptime for inference endpoints.

Proposed dedicated capacity configuration
- Reserved pool: 6 x A100 (40GB) equivalent GPUs initially (config attached: redwood-dedicated-capacity-estimate.xlsx).
- Isolation: Private VPC deployment with customer-managed subnet and KMS integration for key management.
- Scaling plan: 1) steady autoscale to 8 GPUs for scheduled peak windows (using reserved burst credits), 2) short-term burst to shared overflow (hosted pool) as fallback for extreme spikes.
- Model suggestion: 13B quantized variant for most workloads; we recommended a 7B variant for extremely latency-sensitive routes.
- SLA targets: p99 latency target <= 750ms for typical loads, p95 <= 300ms; uptime objective 99.95% with automatic fallbacks.

Deliverables & next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (David) to validate network/KMS and run a quick load profile (I suggested Thu 5/14).
2) We will share a draft term sheet and committed pricing for the reserved capacity (attached).
3) Procurement checklist: we need a PO or signed term sheet and a short security addendum (SOC2 evidence - we can provide a redacted pack).
4) Timeline: with an agreed term we can provision the dedicated pool in ~3 weeks (subject to region availability).

Samir - can you confirm: 1) the target peak timeframe (you mentioned 9-11am PT), and 2) whether Acme requires on-prem air-gapped options or if a customer VPC deployment is sufficient?

Thanks - looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-estimate.xlsx, draft-term-sheet-acme.pdf

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Acme Health

Thanks Marissa - this looks great and captures the discussion. A few quick clarifications: 

- Peak window is indeed 09:00-11:00 PT weekdays; we occasionally have a smaller spike around 19:00 PT.
- VPC deployment is sufficient for now; on-prem air-gapped is not required at this stage, though security will want a checklist.
- For the SLA numbers: p99 <= 750ms is acceptable for our non-critical routes. We do have a handful (~3) of high-priority routes where we need p99 <= 400ms - those would be candidates for the 7B low-latency model or dedicated routing.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll loop in procurement to review the draft term sheet and get an estimate for PO timing.
- Priya will join the technical deep-dive on Thu 5/14.

Appreciate the clear plan - looking forward to the load profile and the term sheet.

Best,
Samir Rao
Head of ML Platforms - Acme Health
samir.rao@acmehealth.com

Looping you both in - Samir confirmed VPC is fine and flagged 3 high-priority routes that need p99 <= 400ms. He and Priya will join the technical deep-dive Thu 5/14.

David - can you prepare a short test plan for the call: 1) network/KMS checklist, 2) quick load profile script (simulate 600 tokens/sec steady + 2.5k burst), 3) perf targets for 13B quantized vs 7B low-latency so we can recommend routing.

Neha - once David gives us a capacity + pricing estimate, can you draft the committed pricing for 6 reserved GPUs + burst capacity and add a note about the SOC2 evidence pack we can send? I've attached the draft term sheet we shared.
